description:
## Diagnosis

A function whose parameter arrives as a lane-form tuple, and whose clause heads destructure it, re-boxes that parameter on entry in order to run its own dispatch.

The argument crosses the call correctly. RuntimeDemand refines a Whole demand on an exact tuple type into TupleFields (src/compiler2/jobs/transport.rs `tuple_refined_demand`), the layout is `ShapeDescr::Tuple` with carrier Absent, artifact.rs flat-maps the lanes into `abi.param_reprs`, and native.rs emits one Var per lane. The callee's entry block therefore has one parameter per field.

Then `lower_clause_dispatch_executable` (src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs:894) forces every dispatch-required input through `materialize_native_value`. For a `NativeBoundValue::Transport { shape: Tuple, lanes }` that is `materialize_transport_value` (native.rs:3787, Tuple arm 3812-3818) -> `Prim::MakeTuple` -> `alloc_struct_for_schema` (native_codegen/prim.rs:258) -> `fz_alloc_struct`. The entry then asks the tuple its arity with a runtime type test and reads the fields back off the heap through `Prim::TupleField` (`dispatch_subject_var`, native.rs:3487, 3515-3519). The clause helpers it tail-calls afterwards operate on the original lanes and allocate nothing. The whole cost is the entry.

The interpreter is a second implementation of the same step with the same defect: `select_clause` (src/ir_interp/backend.rs:702) materializes each required input at line 717 through its own `materialize_transport_value` (backend.rs:2587) and `make_tuple_on_proc` (backend.rs:3173).

The question "field i of this bound value" already has an allocation-free answer for ordinary body steps: `BackendStep::TupleField` (native.rs:1427) goes through `transport_tuple_field` (native.rs:3885) and `transport_field_views` (native.rs:4037), which return lane views. Entry dispatch asks the same question and allocates. One question, two implementations.

There is also dead machinery for exactly this question at the wrong tier: `delivered_tuple_fields` and `emit_delivered_tuple_test` in native_codegen/prim.rs (1024, 1055) answer a tuple type test from delivered field params, reading `body.cache.tuple_field_params`, which nothing ever writes (entry.rs:129 receives it as `_tuple_field_params` and drops it).

## Aggravating case

Extern-free, no Kernel involvement:

    defp pair(n), do: if n > 0, do: {n, false}, else: {n, true}
    defp unwrap({v, false}), do: v
    defp unwrap({_, true}), do: -1

    def main() do
      before = Process.heap_alloc_stats()
      a = unwrap(pair(5))
      b = unwrap(pair(-5))
      later = Process.heap_alloc_stats()
      dbg({a, b})
      dbg({before[:struct_allocs], before[:struct_bytes]})
      dbg({later[:struct_allocs], later[:struct_bytes]})
    end

Measured 2026-09-14, interp and run, identical at main-side commit 4f49465f9 and at fz-5xp.30 head 95c3caa3a:

    {5, -1}
    {0, 0}
    {2, 64}

One 32-byte struct per `unwrap` call. `pair/1` allocates nothing; `unwrap/1` has param_reprs [RawInt, RawAtom] and its entry CLIF opens with the allocator call.

The louder occurrence: fz-5xp.30 makes Kernel arithmetic `def (l :: integer) + (r :: integer), do: arithmetic_result(fz_op_add_ii(l, r))`, where the extern returns a fixed C pair in two lanes and `arithmetic_result/1` destructures `{result, false}` / `{_, true}`. Every arithmetic operation in the language now passes through this entry, so `x + 1` allocates one struct per evaluation. On that branch: enum_list_allocations struct_allocs 0 -> 10 and struct_bytes 0 -> 320 (heap headline 80 -> 400), map_atom_order struct 3/96 -> 12/384, tree 3/144 -> 6/240.

## Signal

All deterministic, no wall clock:

1. The program above as a behavior fixture with heap counters: `{2, 64}` becomes `{0, 0}` on interp, run and build. It is red on main today, which proves the fix addresses the defect and not the arithmetic symptom.
2. A program-walk assertion through `RequestedOutputSink::program` that no dispatch-entry function (`__e*`) contains `Stmt::Let(_, Prim::MakeTuple(_))`. Not a CLIF string match: the allocator renders as `u0:N`, so `contains("fz_alloc_struct")` passes forever. Precedent at jobs/native.rs:5448.
3. `backend_inventory_width_stays_pinned_on_the_target_fixtures` (canon_test.rs) unchanged: lowering changes, identity does not.
4. On the fz-5xp.30 branch after merge, goldens move only downward: enum_list_allocations {5, 80, 10, 320, ...} -> {5, 80, 0, 0, ...} with headline 400 -> 80; map_atom_order struct 12/384 -> 3/96; tree 6/240 -> 3/144.
5. The existing test `entry_dispatch_does_not_materialize_unneeded_structural_inputs` (backend.rs:4054) is the invariant this extends from unneeded inputs to needed lane-form inputs.

## Fix

Entry dispatch becomes lane-aware, using the calculator that already exists. `DispatchState.dispatch_inputs` and `values` carry `NativeBoundValue` instead of `Var`; `dispatch_subject_var` splits into a value form, where `ProjectionKind::TupleField` on a Transport{Tuple} subject is `lanes[i]` and emits nothing, and a Var form used only where a single word is required (guards, MatcherMapGet, BitReaderInit); `Region::TupleArity(n)` over a lane-form subject is a compile-time constant; `Region::Type` over one is answered per field through `transport_field_views`; `lower_argument_bindings` takes bound values. The interpreter's `select_clause` takes the same shape, and the field-view calculator is lifted to one place both doors call so the fix is not made twice.

Deleted in the same motion: `delivered_tuple_fields`, `emit_delivered_tuple_test` and the `tuple_field_params` fast paths in native_codegen/prim.rs; the `tuple_field_params` field and plumbing in entry.rs, env.rs, function.rs. Check whether the MakeTuple-then-TupleField peephole assertions at jobs/native.rs:5448-5456 exist only for this shape.

Not an inliner, not a macro, not an arithmetic-specific lowering. fz-5xp.20 (the ordinary-call inliner) becomes an optimization rather than the remedy for this allocation.

## Where

Predates fz-5xp.30; fix against main in its own session and merge forward into PR #158, where the four goldens above move back down. Docs: .agent/docs/pipeline.md (tuple-field transport), dispatch-matrix.md, pattern-matching.md; the fixture headers of enum_list_allocations (its "a general inliner" sentence becomes false), tree and map_atom_order.

comments.text: Second aggravating case, measured 2026-09-14 on 7123a9061: fixtures2/behavior/tail_recursion.fz (count(100000, 0) with 'count(n - 1, acc + 1)') on the interpreter door takes 4.2s against 1.35s at 4f49465f9; compile is 0.1s of that, the rest is execution. Heap counters around the loop: 200,000 struct allocations on interp and on run (one per + and -), zero at the baseline. The JIT runs the same loop in 0.32s despite the allocations, so on the interpreter the arithmetic route (a Kernel clause call, the extern, an arithmetic_result call whose entry re-boxes the pair) costs about 14us per operation. Consequence: matrix::tail_recursion::interp trips CI's 20s guard under contention (run 34839703161), so PR #158 has a flaky lane until this lands. Signal for the fix: interp time on tail_recursion returns to the baseline's order and struct_allocs is 0 across the loop.

title: Entry dispatch re-boxes a lane-form tuple parameter to destructure it: one heap struct per destructuring call
